main.title: General Data Protection Regulation
main.summary: The General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), abbreviated GDPR, is a European Union regulation on information privacy in the European Union (EU) and the European Economic Area (EEA).

cards.heading: General Data Protection Regulation
cards.text:
The General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), abbreviated GDPR, is a European Union regulation on information privacy in the European Union (EU) and the European Economic Area (EEA). The GDPR is an important component of EU privacy law and human rights law, in particular Article 8(1) of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. It also governs the transfer of personal data outside the EU and EEA. The GDPR's goals are to enhance individuals' control and rights over their personal information and to simplify the regulations for international business. It supersedes the Data Protection Directive 95/46/EC and, among other things, simplifies the terminology.

The European Parliament and Council of the European Union adopted the GDPR on 14 April 2016, to become effective on 25 May 2018. As an EU regulation (instead of a directive), the GDPR has direct legal effect and does not require transposition into national law. However, it also provides flexibility for individual member states to modify (derogate from) some of its provisions.

main.title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald
main.subtitle: Newt enters a struggle over the future of the magical world
main.summary: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald expands Newt Scamander's travels into a conflict over power within the wizarding world. David Yates returns as director, with J.K. Rowling again writing the screenplay. Released in Britain and the United States on 16 November 2018, the sequel introduces Jude Law as a younger Albus Dumbledore.

cards.heading: The conflict spreads
cards.text: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald expands Newt Scamander's travels into a conflict over power within the wizarding world. David Yates returns as director, with J.K. Rowling again writing the screenplay. Released in Britain and the United States on 16 November 2018, the sequel introduces Jude Law as a younger Albus Dumbledore.

cards.heading: A search through Paris
cards.text: Dumbledore asks his former pupil Newt to help oppose Gellert Grindelwald, played by Johnny Depp. The search brings the characters to Paris, where the paths of Newt, Tina, Jacob and Queenie cross with people seeking answers about Credence. Newt's brother Theseus and Leta Lestrange bring their own history into the journey. The movement between these characters makes personal relationships part of the larger struggle, with old loyalties complicating the choices they face in the present.

cards.heading: Choosing a side
cards.text: Grindelwald gathers support by offering a vision of the future that gives his listeners reasons to overlook the violence behind it. Newt's reluctance to fit neatly into competing institutions becomes harder to sustain as that movement grows. The creatures remain part of the action, but their discovery now sits beside questions of allegiance and family history. James Newton Howard returns as composer, adding new themes and the title track to the musical material established in the first film.

main.title: Parasite
main.summary: Bong Joon Ho's Parasite premiered at Cannes on 21 May 2019 and became the first Korean film to win the Palme d'Or.

cards.heading: Parasite
cards.text: Bong Joon Ho's Parasite premiered at Cannes on 21 May 2019 and became the first Korean film to win the Palme d'Or. Its story follows a poor family gradually entering the home and lives of a wealthy household. Bong developed it from an earlier play, working with co-writer Han Jin-won on the screenplay. The film combines black comedy and thriller elements around that unequal relationship. Released in South Korea later that month, it found a worldwide audience, earning about 258 million dollars against a production budget of 11.4 million.

cards.heading: Fridays for Future
cards.text:
Fridays for Future (FFF), also known as the School Strike for Climate (Swedish: Skolstrejk för klimatet [ˈskûːlstrɛjk fœr klɪˈmɑ̌ːtɛt]), is an international movement of school students who skip Friday classes to participate in demonstrations to demand action from political leaders to prevent climate change and for the fossil fuel industry to transition to renewable energy. Publicity and widespread organising began after Swedish pupil Greta Thunberg staged a protest in August 2018 outside of the Swedish parliament, the Riksdag, holding a sign that read "Skolstrejk för klimatet" ("School strike for the climate").

A global strike on 15 March 2019 gathered more than one million strikers in 2,200 strikes organised in 125 countries. On 24 May 2019, in the second global strike, 1,600 protests across 150 countries drew hundreds of thousands of strikers. The May protests were timed to coincide with the 2019 European Parliament election.

main.title: The first image of a black hole
main.summary: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration revealed its image of the black hole in Messier 87 on April 10, 2019.

cards.heading: A planet-sized telescope reveals a shadow
cards.text:
The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration revealed the first image of a black hole on April 10, 2019. It showed a bright ring surrounding the dark shadow of the supermassive black hole in Messier 87, around fifty-five million light-years from Earth.

The result came from combining observations by radio telescopes around the world into a virtual Earth-sized instrument. An international collaboration built through years of technical development, the EHT used that combined resolving power to study structures near a black hole's event horizon.

main.title: Chernobyl
main.subtitle: A disaster drama follows the work of understanding and containing an accident
main.summary: Chernobyl dramatises the 1986 nuclear accident through the people who investigate its cause and attempt to limit the damage. Written by Craig Mazin and directed by Johan Renck, the five-part HBO/Sky miniseries began on HBO in the United States on 6 May 2019. Jared Harris, Stellan Skarsgård and Emily Watson lead a story that moves between technical decisions, official explanations and the cost of emergency work.

cards.heading: The 2019 dramatisation
cards.text: Chernobyl dramatises the 1986 nuclear accident through the people who investigate its cause and attempt to limit the damage. Written by Craig Mazin and directed by Johan Renck, the five-part HBO/Sky miniseries began on HBO in the United States on 6 May 2019. Jared Harris, Stellan Skarsgård and Emily Watson lead a story that moves between technical decisions, official explanations and the cost of emergency work.

cards.heading: Work inside an invisible danger
cards.text: The opening episodes keep immediate confusion close to the physical work around the reactor. Firefighters, plant staff and medical workers encounter a danger that cannot always be recognised through ordinary experience. Scientific knowledge becomes useful only when it can change an order or a procedure. That creates conflict with officials who depend on reassurance and a controlled account of events. The drama repeatedly asks who has enough information to understand a risk and who is being sent to bear it.

cards.heading: Understanding changes responsibility
cards.text: Later episodes connect the emergency response to the investigation of the accident. Mazin's script organises technical explanations around decisions, so a change in the understanding of the reactor also changes the understanding of responsibility. The production was filmed in Lithuania, using spaces that give the work an industrial and domestic setting. Renck's restrained pacing allows an evacuation, a shift or an instruction to gather weight before its consequences become fully apparent.

main.title: Joker
main.subtitle: Arthur Fleck searches for an audience
main.summary: Todd Phillips' Joker builds a film around Arthur Fleck, a struggling Gotham clown who hopes to become a stand-up comedian. Joaquin Phoenix's performance makes his movements, strained laughter and discomfort central to the story. After its Venice premiere on 31 August 2019, the film opened in the United States on 4 October and offered a new origin for Batman's famous adversary.

cards.heading: A clown looking for recognition
cards.text: Todd Phillips' Joker builds a film around Arthur Fleck, a struggling Gotham clown who hopes to become a stand-up comedian. Joaquin Phoenix's performance makes his movements, strained laughter and discomfort central to the story. After its Venice premiere on 31 August 2019, the film opened in the United States on 4 October and offered a new origin for Batman's famous adversary.

cards.heading: The audience Arthur imagines
cards.text: Arthur's working life and ambitions repeatedly bring him before people who dismiss or humiliate him. His attachment to a television host gives him an imagined audience long before he has a real one. Phillips and co-writer Scott Silver keep the story close to Arthur's experience, allowing wishful thinking to enter scenes that initially appear ordinary. As his actions become more violent, public attention gives them a meaning that spreads beyond the man who committed them.

cards.heading: A transformation heard and seen
cards.text: Hildur Guðnadóttir began composing from the screenplay before filming. Her cello-led score places Arthur's unease beneath the images, and music already written for the production helped shape Phoenix's bathroom dance. That scene turns a private physical gesture into a moment of transformation. The partnership between score and performance is one of the film's defining choices: Arthur's body can express a change before he explains it. Joker received the Golden Lion at Venice.

main.title: Apple M1
main.summary: The Apple M1 is a series of ARM-based system-on-a-chip (SoC) designed by Apple Inc., launched in 2020.

cards.heading: Apple M1
cards.text: The Apple M1 is a series of ARM-based system-on-a-chip (SoC) designed by Apple Inc., launched in 2020. It is part of the Apple silicon series, as a central processing unit (CPU) and graphics processing unit (GPU), used for its Mac desktops and notebooks and iPad Pro and iPad Air tablets. The M1 chip initiated Apple's third change to the instruction set architecture used by Macintosh computers, switching from Intel to Apple silicon fourteen years after they switched from PowerPC to Intel, and twenty-six years after their transition from the Motorola 68000 series to PowerPC. At the time of its introduction in 2020, Apple said that the M1 had "the world's fastest CPU core in low power silicon" and the world's best CPU performance per watt. Its successor, Apple M2, was announced on June 6, 2022, at its Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC).

main.title: COVID-19 pandemic
main.summary: COVID-19 spread worldwide in early 2020 after an outbreak identified in Wuhan in December 2019.

cards.heading: COVID-19 pandemic
cards.text: COVID-19 spread worldwide in early 2020 after an outbreak identified in Wuhan in December 2019. The World Health Organization declared an international health emergency on 30 January and described the outbreak as a pandemic on 11 March. Airborne transmission helped the virus spread, while new variants altered patterns of infection. Vaccines were developed rapidly and began reaching the public in December 2020 through national and international programmes. The WHO ended the international emergency in May 2023, while continuing to recognise COVID-19 as a global health threat.

main.title: George Floyd protests
main.summary: Protests, riots, and demonstrations against police brutality began in Minneapolis in the United States on May 26, 2020 as reactions to the murder of George Floyd, a 46-year-old unarmed African American man, by city police during an arrest.

cards.heading: George Floyd protests
cards.text:
Protests, riots, and demonstrations against police brutality began in Minneapolis in the United States on May 26, 2020 as reactions to the murder of George Floyd, a 46-year-old unarmed African American man, by city police during an arrest. They spread nationally and internationally. Veteran officer Derek Chauvin was recorded as kneeling on Floyd's neck for 9 minutes and 29 seconds; Floyd complained of not being able to breathe, but three other officers looked on and prevented passersby from intervening. Chauvin and the other three officers involved were fired and later arrested. In April 2021, Chauvin was found guilty of second-degree murder, third-degree murder, and second-degree manslaughter. In June 2021, Chauvin was sentenced to 22+1⁄2 years in prison.

The George Floyd protest movement began hours after his murder as bystander video and word of mouth began to spread. Protests first emerged at the East 38th and Chicago Avenue street intersection in Minneapolis, the location of Floyd's arrest and murder, and other sites in the Minneapolis–Saint Paul metropolitan area of Minnesota.
